sanskrit: putratvam abhigacchāva tava caiva sulocana vara eṣa vṛto deva tad viddhi surasattama
english: We shall both become your sons, O beautiful-eyed one. This is the boon chosen, O God; know it thus, O best among the gods.

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca bāḍham evaṃ kariṣyāmi sarvam etad bhaviṣyati
english: The Lord said: So be it. I shall do exactly this; all of it shall come to pass.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca vicintya tv atha govindo nāpaśyad yad anāvṛtam avakāśaṃ pṛthivyāṃ vā divi vā madhusūdanaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then Govinda, the slayer of Madhu, reflected and found no unoccupied spot — neither on earth nor in heaven.

sanskrit: svakāv anāvṛtāv ūrū dṛṣṭvā devavaras tadā madhukaiṭabhayo rājañ śirasī madhusūdanaḥ cakreṇa śitadhāreṇa nyakṛntata mahāyaśāḥ
english: Then, O king, the best of gods, the greatly glorious Madhusūdana, seeing his own thighs unsubmerged, severed the heads of Madhu and Kaiṭabha there with his sharp-edged discus.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca dhundhur nāma mahātejās tayoḥ putro mahādyutiḥ sa tapo 'tapyata mahan mahāvīryaparākramaḥ
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: The son of those two was Dhundhu by name, of great energy and great splendour. He performed great austerities, possessed of mighty valour and prowess.

sanskrit: atiṣṭhad ekapādena kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ tasmai brahmā dadau prīto varaṃ vavre sa ca prabho
english: He stood on one foot, emaciated, his veins protruding. Brahmā, pleased, gave him a boon, and he asked for a boon, O lord.

sanskrit: devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ sarpagandharvarakṣasām avadhyo 'haṃ bhaveyaṃ vai vara eṣa vṛto mayā
english: "May I be invincible to gods, dānavas, yakṣas, serpents, gandharvas, and rākṣasas — this is the boon I have chosen."

sanskrit: evaṃ bhavatu gaccheti tam uvāca pitāmahaḥ sa evam uktas tatpādau mūrdhnā spṛśya jagāma ha
english: "So be it; go," said the Grandfather to him. Thus addressed, he touched the Grandfather's feet with his head and departed.

sanskrit: sa tu dhundhur varaṃ labdhvā mahāvīryaparākramaḥ anusmaran pitṛvadhaṃ tato viṣṇum upādravat
english: Then Dhundhu, of mighty valour and prowess, having obtained the boon, remembering the slaying of his fathers, attacked Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: sa tu devān sagandharvāñ jitvā dhundhur amarṣaṇaḥ babādha sarvān asakṛd devān viṣṇuṃ ca vai bhṛśam
english: The wrathful Dhundhu, having conquered the gods together with the gandharvas, again and again oppressed all the gods and Viṣṇu greatly.

sanskrit: samudro vālukāpūrṇa ujjānaka iti smṛtaḥ āgamya ca sa duṣṭātmā taṃ deśaṃ bharatarṣabha bādhate sma paraṃ śaktyā tam uttaṅkāśramaṃ prabho
english: That ocean filled with sand is known as Ujjānaka. Coming to that region, O bull of the Bhāratas, the evil-souled one oppressed with utmost force the hermitage of Uttaṅka, O lord.

sanskrit: antarbhūmigatas tatra vālukāntarhitas tadā madhukaiṭabhayoḥ putro dhundhur bhīmaparākramaḥ
english: There, having gone underground and concealed within the sand, Dhundhu, son of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, of terrible prowess,

sanskrit: śete lokavināśāya tapobalasamāśritaḥ uttaṅkasyāśramābhyāśe niḥśvasan pāvakārciṣaḥ
english: lay sleeping, sustained by the power of his austerities, for the destruction of the worlds, near the hermitage of Uttaṅka, breathing out flames of fire.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ kuvalāśvo narapatir anvito balaśālinām
english: At this very time, King Kuvalāśva, accompanied by his retinue, army, and conveyances, attended by thousands of mighty warriors,

sanskrit: sahasrair ekaviṃśatyā putrāṇām arimardanaḥ prāyād uttaṅkasahito dhundhos tasya niveśanam
english: twenty-one thousand sons, the crusher of foes, went together with Uttaṅka to the abode of that Dhundhu.

sanskrit: tam āviśat tato viṣṇur bhagavāṃs tejasā prabhuḥ uttaṅkasya niyogena lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: Then the Lord Viṣṇu entered him with his radiance, at Uttaṅka's bidding, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.

sanskrit: tasmin prayāte durdharṣe divi śabdo mahān abhūt eṣa śrīmān nṛpasuto dhundhumāro bhaviṣyati
english: When that invincible one set forth, a great sound arose in heaven: "This glorious prince shall become Dhundhumāra."

sanskrit: divyaiś ca puṣpais taṃ devāḥ samantāt paryavākiran devadundubhayaś caiva neduḥ svayam udīritāḥ
english: The gods showered him on all sides with divine flowers, and the celestial kettledrums sounded of their own accord.

sanskrit: śītaś ca vāyuḥ pravavau prayāṇe tasya dhīmataḥ vipāṃsulāṃ mahīṃ kurvan vavarṣa ca sureśvaraḥ
english: A cool wind blew at the departure of that wise one, purifying the earth, and the lord of the gods rained down.

sanskrit: antarikṣe vimānāni devatānāṃ yudhiṣṭhira tatraiva samadṛśyanta dhundhur yatra mahāsuraḥ
english: In the sky, O Yudhiṣṭhira, the celestial chariots of the gods became visible right there where the great asura Dhundhu was.

sanskrit: kuvalāśvasya dhundhoś ca yuddhakautūhalānvitāḥ devagandharvasahitāḥ samavaikṣan maharṣayaḥ
english: The great sages, filled with eagerness to see the battle of Kuvalāśva and Dhundhu, together with the gods and gandharvas, watched.

sanskrit: nārāyaṇena kauravya tejasāpyāyitas tadā sa gato nṛpatiḥ kṣipraṃ putrais taiḥ sarvatodiśam
english: Invigorated by the energy of Nārāyaṇa, O descendant of the Kurus, that king quickly went in all directions with those sons.

sanskrit: arṇavaṃ khānayām āsa kuvalāśvo mahīpatiḥ kuvalāśvasya putrais tu tasmin vai vālukārṇave
english: King Kuvalāśva caused the sandy ocean to be dug; and indeed in that ocean of sand, by the sons of Kuvalāśva,

sanskrit: saptabhir divasaiḥ khātvā dṛṣṭo dhundhur mahābalaḥ āsīd ghoraṃ vapus tasya vālukāntarhitaṃ mahat dīpyamānaṃ yathā sūryas tejasā bharatarṣabha
english: after digging for seven days, the mighty Dhundhu was seen. His body, vast and terrible, concealed within the sand, blazed like the sun in its energy, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tato dhundhur mahārāja diśam āśritya paścimām supto 'bhūd rājaśārdūla kālānalasamadyutiḥ
english: Then, O great king, O tiger among kings, Dhundhu lay sleeping, turned toward the western quarter, blazing like the fire of universal dissolution.

sanskrit: kuvalāśvasya putrais tu sarvataḥ parivāritaḥ abhidrutaḥ śarais tīkṣṇair gadābhir musalair api paṭṭiśaiḥ parighaiḥ prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiś ca vimalaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: Surrounded on all sides by the sons of Kuvalāśva, he was rushed upon and struck with sharp arrows, clubs, pestles, halberds, iron bars, javelins, and bright sharp swords.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ saṃkruddhaḥ samuttasthau mahābalaḥ kruddhaś cābhakṣayat teṣāṃ śastrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: Struck thus, the mighty one arose in great fury, and in his rage consumed their various weapons.

sanskrit: āsyād vaman pāvakaṃ sa saṃvartakasamaṃ tadā tān sarvān nṛpateḥ putrān adahat svena tejasā
english: Vomiting fire from his mouth comparable to the fire of the end of time, he burned all the king's sons with his own energy.

sanskrit: mukhajenāgninā kruddho lokān udvartayann iva kṣaṇena rājaśārdūla pureva kapilaḥ prabhuḥ sagarasyātmajān kruddhas tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: With the fire born from his mouth, enraged, as if overturning the worlds, O tiger among kings, in an instant — just as Kapila the lord had in former times burned the sons of Sagara in his fury — that too seemed like a wonder.

sanskrit: teṣu krodhāgnidagdheṣu tadā bharatasattama taṃ prabuddhaṃ mahātmānaṃ kumbhakarṇam ivāparam āsasāda mahātejāḥ kuvalāśvo mahīpatiḥ
english: When they were burned by the fire of his wrath, O best of the Bhāratas, the greatly energetic King Kuvalāśva approached that awakened great-souled one, who was like another Kumbhakarṇa.

sanskrit: tasya vāri mahārāja susrāva bahu dehataḥ tadāpīyata tat tejo rājā vārimayaṃ nṛpa yogī yogena vahniṃ ca śamayām āsa vāriṇā
english: From his body, O great king, much water flowed abundantly; then the king, that yogi, absorbed that fiery energy made of water, O king, and by yoga extinguished the fire with water.

sanskrit: brahmāstreṇa tadā rājā daityaṃ krūraparākramam dadāha bharataśreṣṭha sarvalokābhayāya vai
english: Then the king burned the demon of cruel valour with the Brahmā-weapon, O best of the Bhāratas, for the sake of fearlessness for all the worlds.

sanskrit: so 'streṇa dagdhvā rājarṣiḥ kuvalāśvo mahāsuram suraśatrum amitraghnas trilokeśa ivāparaḥ dhundhumāra iti khyāto nāmnā samabhavat tataḥ
english: Having burned that great demon, the enemy of the gods, with his weapon, the royal sage Kuvalāśva, slayer of foes, like another lord of the three worlds, thenceforth became known by the name Dhundhumāra — "slayer of Dhundhu."

sanskrit: prītaiś ca tridaśaiḥ sarvair maharṣisahitais tadā varaṃ vṛṇīṣvety uktaḥ sa prāñjaliḥ praṇatas tadā atīva mudito rājann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then, told "choose a boon" by all the delighted gods together with the great sages, he stood with joined palms, bowed down, exceedingly joyful, O king, and spoke these words:

sanskrit: dadyāṃ vittaṃ dvijāgryebhyaḥ śatrūṇāṃ cāpi durjayaḥ sakhyaṃ ca viṣṇunā me syād bhūteṣv adroha eva ca dharme ratiś ca satataṃ svarge vāsas tathākṣayaḥ
english: "May I give wealth to the foremost brahmins, and may I be unconquerable by enemies; may friendship with Viṣṇu be mine, and non-injury to all beings; may there be constant delight in righteousness, and an eternal dwelling in heaven."

sanskrit: tathāstv iti tato devaiḥ prītair uktaḥ sa pārthivaḥ ṛṣibhiś ca sagandharvair uttaṅkena ca dhīmatā
english: "So be it" — thus was that king told by the delighted gods, by the sages together with the gandharvas, and by the wise Uttaṅka.

sanskrit: sabhājya cainaṃ vividhair āśīrvādais tato nṛpam devā maharṣayaś caiva svāni sthānāni bhejire
english: Having honoured that king with various blessings, the gods and the great sages then departed to their own abodes.

sanskrit: tasya putrās trayaḥ śiṣṭā yudhiṣṭhira tadābhavan dṛḍhāśvaḥ kapilāśvaś ca candrāśvaś caiva bhārata tebhyaḥ paramparā rājann ikṣvākūṇāṃ mahātmanām
english: Three of his sons remained surviving, O Yudhiṣṭhira: Dṛḍhāśva, Kapilāśva, and Candrāśva, O Bhārata. From them, O king, descended in succession the great-souled Ikṣvāku kings.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa nihatas tena kuvalāśvena sattama dhundhur daityo mahāvīryo madhukaiṭabhayoḥ sutaḥ
english: Thus was Dhundhu the daitya, of great valour, son of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, slain by that Kuvalāśva, O excellent one.

sanskrit: kuvalāśvas tu nṛpatir dhundhumāra iti smṛtaḥ nāmnā ca guṇasaṃyuktas tadā prabhṛti so 'bhavat
english: And King Kuvalāśva became known as Dhundhumāra, endowed with that name along with its qualities from that time forth.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi dhaundhumāram upākhyānaṃ prathitaṃ yasya karmaṇā
english: All of this that you asked me has been narrated — the celebrated tale of Dhundhumāra, famous by reason of his deeds.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu puṇyam ākhyānaṃ viṣṇoḥ samanukīrtanam śṛṇuyād yaḥ sa dharmātmā putravāṃś ca bhaven naraḥ
english: This holy narrative, which is also a glorification of Viṣṇu — whoever hears it shall be righteous-souled and shall have sons.

sanskrit: āyuṣmān dhṛtimāṃś caiva śrutvā bhavati parvasu na ca vyādhibhayaṃ kiṃ cit prāpnoti vigatajvaraḥ
english: He becomes long-lived and steadfast upon hearing it at the sacred days; nor does he encounter any fear of disease, freed from fever.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā mārkaṇḍeyaṃ mahādyutim papraccha bharataśreṣṭho dharmapraśnaṃ sudurvacam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, the best of the Bhāratas, asked Mārkaṇḍeya of great brilliance a question on dharma most difficult to answer.

sanskrit: śrotum icchāmi bhagavan strīṇāṃ māhātmyam uttamam kathyamānaṃ tvayā vipra sūkṣmaṃ dharmaṃ ca tattvataḥ
english: "I desire to hear, O Lord, the supreme greatness of women as narrated by you, O brahmin, and the subtle dharma as it truly is."

sanskrit: pratyakṣeṇa hi viprarṣe devā dṛśyanti sattama sūryācandramasau vāyuḥ pṛthivī vahnir eva ca
english: "For directly visible, O brahmin-sage, O excellent one, are the gods — the sun and moon, wind, earth, and fire."

sanskrit: pitā mātā ca bhagavan gāva eva ca sattama yac cānyad eva vihitaṃ tac cāpi bhṛgunandana
english: "Father and mother, O Lord, and cows too, O excellent one, and whatever else is ordained — all that too, O joy of the Bhṛgu line."

sanskrit: manye 'haṃ guruvat sarvam ekapatnyas tathā striyaḥ pativratānāṃ śuśrūṣā duṣkarā pratibhāti me
english: "I regard all of these as like a teacher; and devoted wives — the service of chaste women to their husbands seems difficult to me."

sanskrit: pativratānāṃ māhātmyaṃ vaktum arhasi naḥ prabho nirudhya cendriyagrāmaṃ manaḥ saṃrudhya cānagha patiṃ daivatavac cāpi cintayantyaḥ sthitā hi yāḥ
english: "Pray tell us the greatness of chaste wives, O lord, O sinless one — those who, restraining the entire host of the senses, controlling the mind, and regarding their husband as a god, remain steadfast."

sanskrit: bhagavan duṣkaraṃ hy etat pratibhāti mama prabho mātāpitṛṣu śuśrūṣā strīṇāṃ bhartṛṣu ca dvija
english: "O Lord, this seems difficult to me, O master: the service of women toward their fathers and mothers, and toward their husbands, O brahmin."

sanskrit: strīṇāṃ dharmāt sughorād dhi nānyaṃ paśyāmi duṣkaram sādhv ācārāḥ striyo brahman yat kurvanti sadādṛtāḥ duṣkaraṃ bata kurvanti pitaro mātaraś ca vai
english: "Indeed I see nothing more difficult than the most severe dharma of women — what women of good conduct, O brahmin, perform with constant reverence. Alas, both fathers and mothers perform what is difficult."

sanskrit: ekapatnyaś ca yā nāryo yāś ca satyaṃ vadanty uta kukṣiṇā daśa māsāṃś ca garbhaṃ saṃdhārayanti yāḥ nāryaḥ kālena saṃbhūya kim adbhutataraṃ tataḥ
english: "And those women who are faithful to one husband, who speak the truth, who carry a child in the womb for ten months — women who, brought together in time, what is more wonderful than that?"

sanskrit: saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ prāpya vedanām atulām api prajāyante sutān nāryo duḥkhena mahatā vibho puṣṇanti cāpi mahatā snehena dvijasattama
english: "Facing the greatest peril and unequalled pain, women bring forth sons with great suffering, O lord, and nourish them too with great love, O best of brahmins."

sanskrit: ye ca krūreṣu sarveṣu vartamānā jugupsitāḥ svakarma kurvanti sadā duṣkaraṃ tac ca me matam
english: "And those who, engaged in all the harsh duties, blameless, always perform their own duty — that too I consider difficult."

sanskrit: kṣatradharmasamācāraṃ tathyaṃ cākhyāhi me dvija dharmaḥ sudurlabho vipra nṛśaṃsena durātmanā
english: "Tell me truly also the practice of the kṣatriya dharma, O brahmin. Dharma is very difficult to attain, O brahmin, by the cruel-natured and evil-souled."

sanskrit: etad icchāmi bhagavan praśnaṃ praśnavidāṃ vara śrotuṃ bhṛgukulaśreṣṭha śuśrūṣe tava suvrata
english: "This I desire, O Lord, O best among those who know questions, to hear from the best of the Bhṛgu lineage. I am eager to attend upon you, O one of good vows."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca hanta te sarvam ākhyāsye praśnam etaṃ sudurvacam tattvena bharataśreṣṭha gadatas tan nibodha me
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Well then, I shall narrate all of this question most difficult to answer, truly, O best of the Bhāratas. Listen to me as I speak.

sanskrit: mātaraṃ sadṛśīṃ tāta pitṝn anye ca manyate duṣkaraṃ kurute mātā vivardhayati yā prajāḥ
english: "Some regard the mother as equal to, dear child, and others regard fathers; the mother does what is hard, she who nurtures offspring."

sanskrit: tapasā devatejyābhir vandanena titikṣayā abhicārair upāyaiś ca īhante pitaraḥ sutān
english: "Through austerities, worship of the gods, salutation, forbearance, and by rites and means, fathers strive for sons."

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛcchreṇa mahatā putraṃ prāpya sudurlabham cintayanti sadā vīra kīdṛśo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Thus, having with great hardship obtained a son so difficult to get, they always think, O hero: 'How will this one turn out?'"

sanskrit: āśaṃsate ca putreṣu pitā mātā ca bhārata yaśaḥ kīrtim athaiśvaryaṃ prajā dharmaṃ tathaiva ca
english: "Both father and mother hope from their sons, O Bhārata, for glory, fame, prosperity, offspring, and dharma as well."

sanskrit: tayor āśāṃ tu saphalāṃ yaḥ karoti sa dharmavit pitā mātā ca rājendra tuṣyato yasya nityadā iha pretya ca tasyātha kīrtir dharmaś ca śāśvataḥ
english: "He who fulfils that hope of theirs is truly the knower of dharma. He whose father and mother are always pleased — both here and hereafter his glory and dharma are eternal."

sanskrit: naiva yajñaḥ striyaḥ kaś cin na śrāddhaṃ nopavāsakam yā tu bhartari śuśrūṣā tayā svargam upāśnute
english: "There is no sacrifice for women, nor any śrāddha, nor any fast. But she who renders service to her husband — by that she attains heaven."

sanskrit: etat prakaraṇaṃ rājann adhikṛtya yudhiṣṭhira prativratānāṃ niyataṃ dharmaṃ cāvahitaḥ śṛṇu
english: "Regarding this topic, O king Yudhiṣṭhira, listen attentively to the fixed dharma of devoted wives."

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca kaś cid dvijātipravaro vedādhyāyī tapodhanaḥ tapasvī dharmaśīlaś ca kauśiko nāma bhārata
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: There was a certain excellent brahmin, a student of the Vedas, rich in austerity, an ascetic, virtuous in conduct, named Kauśika, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sāṅgopaniṣadān vedān adhīte dvijasattamaḥ sa vṛkṣamūle kasmiṃś cid vedān uccārayan sthitaḥ
english: That best of brahmins studied the Vedas together with their limbs and Upaniṣads. He stood at the foot of a certain tree, reciting the Vedas aloud.

sanskrit: upariṣṭāc ca vṛkṣasya balākā saṃnyalīyata tayā purīṣam utsṛṣṭaṃ brāhmaṇasya tadopari
english: A crane settled in the tree above him, and it dropped its excrement upon the brahmin.

sanskrit: tām avekṣya tataḥ kruddhaḥ samapadhyāyata dvijaḥ bhṛśaṃ krodhābhibhūtena balākā sā nirīkṣitā
english: Looking up at it, the brahmin became angry and glared at it. Utterly overcome by wrath, he stared at that crane.

sanskrit: apadhyātā ca vipreṇa nyapatad vasudhātale balākāṃ patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā gatasattvām acetanām kāruṇyād abhisaṃtaptaḥ paryaśocata tāṃ dvijaḥ
english: Cursed by the brahmin's angry gaze, it fell to the ground. Seeing the crane fallen, drained of life, unconscious, the brahmin was filled with compassion and lamented for it.

sanskrit: akāryaṃ kṛtavān asmi rāgadveṣabalātkṛtaḥ ity uktvā bahuśo vidvān grāmaṃ bhaikṣāya saṃśritaḥ
english: "I have done a wrongful deed, overcome by the force of passion and hatred" — saying this repeatedly, the learned one went to the village to beg alms.

sanskrit: grāme śucīni pracaran kulāni bharatarṣabha praviṣṭas tat kulaṃ yatra pūrvaṃ caritavāṃs tu saḥ
english: Moving through the respectable households of the village, O bull of the Bhāratas, he entered the very household where he had formerly begged.

sanskrit: dehīti yācamāno vai tiṣṭhety uktaḥ striyā tataḥ śaucaṃ tu yāvat kurute bhājanasya kuṭumbinī
english: Saying "Give!" and begging, he was told "Wait" by a woman there, while the housewife was performing the cleansing of her vessels.

sanskrit: etasminn antare rājan kṣudhāsaṃpīḍito bhṛśam bhartā praviṣṭaḥ sahasā tasyā bharatasattama
english: In the meantime, O king, O best of the Bhāratas, her husband suddenly arrived, greatly afflicted by hunger.

sanskrit: sā tu dṛṣṭvā patiṃ sādhvī brāhmaṇaṃ vyapahāya tam pādyam ācamanīyaṃ ca dadau bhartre tathāsanam
english: But that virtuous woman, seeing her husband, set aside that brahmin and gave water for washing feet, water for sipping, and a seat to her husband.

sanskrit: prahvā paryacarac cāpi bhartāram asitekṣaṇā āhāreṇātha bhakṣyaiś ca vākyaiḥ sumadhurais tathā
english: The dark-eyed one bowed reverently and served her husband with food, eatables, and very sweet words.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭaṃ bhuñjate bhartuḥ sā tu nityaṃ yudhiṣṭhira daivataṃ ca patiṃ mene bhartuś cittānusāriṇī
english: She always ate the remnants of her husband's meal, O Yudhiṣṭhira, and she regarded her husband as a god, ever following the mind of her husband.

sanskrit: na karmaṇā na manasā nātyaśnān nāpi cāpibat taṃ sarvabhāvopagatā patiśuśrūṣaṇe ratā
english: Neither in deed nor in mind did she transgress him; she neither overate nor drank excessively; devoted to him with all her heart, she was intent on serving her husband.

sanskrit: sādhvācārā śucir dakṣā kuṭumbasya hitaiṣiṇī bhartuś cāpi hitaṃ yat tat satataṃ sānuvartate
english: Of good conduct, pure, capable, devoted to the welfare of the household — whatever was the welfare of her husband, she constantly pursued that.

sanskrit: devatātithibhṛtyānāṃ śvaśrūśvaśurayos tathā śuśrūṣaṇaparā nityaṃ satataṃ saṃyatendriyā
english: Always intent on serving gods, guests, servants, and likewise mother-in-law and father-in-law, with senses ever restrained.

sanskrit: sā brāhmaṇaṃ tadā dṛṣṭvā saṃsthitaṃ bhaikṣakāṅkṣiṇam kurvatī patiśuśrūṣāṃ sasmārātha śubhekṣaṇā
english: Then she, the bright-eyed one, while engaged in serving her husband, saw the brahmin standing there waiting for alms, and remembered him.
